chapter: Imperial Orchestra and Southern Rhythm Boys
title: Church disapproval of jazz and her mother's feelings
summary: Church women said the little girl was going to hell for playing jazz; her father backed her, while her mother worried because she was young and had washed laundry to pay for lessons.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And I shall never forget, there were certain women, like older women at the church, you know, they just thought it was awful. Finally, when my mother did consent to let me play in the orchestra with my dad, you know, and Mr. Hartz, they said, "I think it's awful for that little girl." "That little girl is playing jazz music, and I think it's terrible. She's going to hell."

"I don't think it's right. I don't think her mother and father should let her do this." So of course my mother felt very bad about it, but my dad didn't, and my dad said, "Listen, she's my daughter and I want her to play. She's got talent, she's got ability and I want her to use it.
I want her to play." And so he just didn't pay any attention to them, and I didn't pay any attention to them either, you know, but my mother, she felt a little funny about it, you know.
Well, did your mother feel funny because it was jazz music or because you were a little girl out there in an orchestra?

I guess it was because I was a little girl, because I was young, you know, and my mother loved me, naturally, like any mother, she was proud of the fact that I could play, because she really -- she used to even wash and iron for my music teacher to be sure that my lessons were paid for, you know. She did that because my dad, as I say, he wasn't making a lot of money. But she did that to help. And she was a beautiful laundress anyway, and as a girl that's what she did, she worked in a Chinese laundry and learned how to do beautiful laundry work. So she would do this sometimes in exchange for my music lessons, for my teacher.
